inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, consolidated cash flow statement 'Equity-settled share-based payments' RMB161,392k (6181.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:5501); equity-award taxes nil (RSU scheme settles in newly issued H shares, no net-share withholding disclosed). H1 FY2026 interim: RMB49,282k.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1746, Yahoo CNYHKD=X regular close 2026-10-23T13:46Z. Statements and all flows are RMB (CNY); the H-share quote is HKD. Per-share values are computed in CNY and multiplied by fx_rate into HKD; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD so they compare to current_price, with *_cny twins for the statement basis. No A-share or ADR dual listing exists for a parity check; the rate was cross-checked against the USD legs (USDHKD / USDCNY) at build time.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares for H1 FY2026, 176,856,191 (interim report note 9, 6181.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:2075); shares in issue 176,744,500 at 30 June 2026. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged once. The two 2025 H-share placements (HK$2.7bn May 2025, ~HK$2.7bn October 2025) are already in the count; a further inventory-funding placement is a bear-case risk noted in the narrative, not modelled as issuance.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8%; China equity risk premium ~6.5%; beta ~1.3 for a single-brand discretionary-luxury retailer gives cost of equity ~10.3%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~3.0% (bank loans priced 1.93-4.75%, FY2025 AR note), ~2.3% after 24% tax; debt is ~8% of enterprise value at the current price (net debt RMB4.15bn vs ~RMB43bn market cap). CAPM WACC ~9.6%, rounded UP to 10.5% to carry ~1pp of size / free-float / HKEX-China-equity liquidity premium. The demand-cycle, gold-price and single-brand operating risks are charged in the scenario paths and the 30% bear weight, NOT in WACC, and the same 10.5% is used in all three scenarios so risk is charged exactly once.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The capitalised (IFRS 16) lease payment, principal RMB234.5m + interest RMB15.6m = RMB250.0m in FY2025 (0.92% of revenue; H1 FY2026 RMB149.8m, 0.76%), is deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (RMB339.4m at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 PP&E depreciation RMB78.8m + amortisation RMB38.0m = RMB116.8m (0.43% of revenue), ROU depreciation RMB222.4m excluded. The far larger variable mall rents ('lease payments not included in the measurement of lease liabilities', RMB1,212.5m in H1 FY2026 alone, ~6% of revenue) are already in selling expenses and therefore already inside the EBITDA margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. All equity is attributable to owners of the parent (interim balance sheet: Total equity = Equity attributable to owners RMB13,224m); no non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon, with the non-US adaptations (CNY WACC, lease treatment B, CNY/HKD dual currency). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: an operating consumer-luxury retailer, not a bank/REIT/LIC. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). ANCHORS: price is the 2026-10-23 HKEX regular close; net debt and share count from the 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet. FY0 = FY2025 (last audited year). The H1 FY2026 owner FCF of ~RMB1.9bn that is already inside the June balance sheet was almost entirely paid out as the FY2025 final dividend (RMB1,692m paid in H1 FY2026), so the June net debt is approximately neutral with respect to the year-1 flow being modelled; the overlap is small and noted rather than adjusted. LAST_FCF: FY2025 owner FCF is -RMB7,155m (reported FCF -RMB6,993m less SBC RMB161m) because inventories rose RMB11,957m (RMB4,088m -> RMB16,044m) in a deliberate gold stockpile funded by RMB6.26bn of new bank borrowings and two H-share placements. It is an inventory-build-distorted base and is NOT used as the projection anchor: the forward build is from components (EBITDA margin, lease, D&A, tax, capex, and working capital at -45% of the revenue CHANGE), which is what the mid-cycle view requires. TTM reported FCF to June 2026 is -RMB2,783m; H1 FY2026 alone +RMB1,937m as growth slowed and inventory build moderated. INTEREST INCOME: RMB3.8m, not stripped, because the company is in a net-debt position (the strip is for net-cash balance sheets). BUYBACKS: none; the flat share count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for, although it does pay large dividends (FY2025 RMB1,096m; H1 FY2026 RMB1,692m). WORKING CAPITAL: net working capital (inventory 19,018 + receivables 524 + prepayments 785 - trade payables 573 - other payables 2,518 - contract liabilities 20) is ~RMB17.2bn, ~50% of TTM revenue, almost all gold inventory at 271 inventory days; the -45% capture on the revenue change means growth consumes cash and a revenue decline releases it, which is the economic reality of a fixed-price gold retailer. SBC: 0.59% of FY2025 revenue, 0.25% in H1 FY2026, projected at 0.35-0.40%; the house/street band is therefore narrow but not collapsed (band_position is meaningful).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2025->FY2035 revenue CAGR (27,303 -> 42,515); the historical CAGRs are a one-off step change (revenue 1.29bn -> 27.3bn in three years) and are not a usable forward proxy
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs exceed 90%/yr and diverge from each other by far more than 30pp (revenue 176% vs EPS 245% vs equity 134% over 3 years); they describe the FY2023-FY2025 heritage-gold boom, not a repeatable rate. H1 FY2026 revenue growth was 60.3% against a 221% comparative, and sell-side tracking (Goldman Sachs) shows Tmall sales -63% YoY in Q2 FY2026. The base case therefore normalises revenue DOWN in FY2027 and compounds at 4.5%/yr over the decade.
historical_growth.notes: Only FY2021-FY2025 annual data exist (listed June 2024), so 5-year CAGRs are unavailable; 4-year CAGRs (FY2021 base) are given instead. Owner FCF: FY2023 -RMB97m, FY2024 -RMB1,328m, FY2025 -RMB7,155m (reported FCF less SBC): negative at both ends of every window, so no FCF CAGR is computable. SBC grew from RMB8.6m (FY2023) to RMB161.4m (FY2025) but remained under 0.6% of revenue; the owner-FCF deterioration is inventory, not SBC.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +24.5% = H1 actual RMB19,808m plus an H2 of ~RMB14.2bn, roughly 5% below the RMB14,949m H2 FY2025 base (brokers flag H2 same-store declines; Q2 online tracking -63%). FY2027 -12% is the normalisation year: the gold-as-investment and reseller demand that inflated FY2025 (SSS +160.6%) unwinds with gold >25% off its early-2026 high and the brand premium over spot at ~60% (Citi). From FY2028 growth is store-driven: 10-12 relocations to larger sites, 6-9 overseas boutiques, goldware category, loyalty base 730k (+20% HoH); 5-6% fading to 3.5%. Mid-cycle productivity implied is ~RMB550-650m per boutique, versus ~RMB1bn in FY2025.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 28.0%: H1 ran 29.7% on low-cost 2025 inventory and the February price rise; H2 compresses as that inventory sells through and gold weakness forces promotion. FY2027-28 24-24.5%: gross margin ~39% (FY2021-24 ran 41-42%, FY2025 37.6% at peak gold inflation, H1 FY2026 41.3%) less ~14-15% opex including ~6% variable mall rent on a lower revenue base. Drifts to 25% as the overseas store base matures; never back to the H1 FY2026 peak.
base.wc_rationale: Net working capital is ~50% of TTM revenue (gold inventory, 271 days). Incremental capture of -45% means each RMB1 of added revenue absorbs RMB0.45 of cash, and the FY2027 revenue decline releases ~RMB1.5bn as purchasing is throttled; FY2024-25 capture was 55-65% during the deliberate stockpile, so -45% assumes modestly less intensity as growth slows.

bull.growth_rationale: H2 FY2026 holds at ~RMB16.8bn (+12% on the H2 FY2025 base) as the Q2 online air-pocket proves to be reseller destocking rather than end demand; FY2027 +5% with no normalisation year; overseas (HK/Macau/Singapore, then Japan, North America, Middle East) and the goldware category sustain 7-8% through FY2030. Still ends at 4% nominal, not a hypergrowth re-acceleration.

bear.growth_rationale: H2 FY2026 falls ~18% on the base (RMB12.1bn) as gold's correction widens the fixed-price premium over by-weight competitors and price-sensitive buyers defect; FY2027 -25% and FY2028 -8% take revenue back to ~RMB22bn (still 2.6x FY2024), a boom that half-reverses. Thereafter a 45-55 boutique luxury franchise growing 2.5-3%: the brand survives, the 2025 step-change does not.
bear.margin_rationale: Gross margin to ~36% (inventory write-downs on RMB19bn of gold bought at 2025 prices, promotional pricing to hold volume) against a largely fixed store-staff and flagship-rent base; EBITDA margin 18-19%, which is still above the FY2023 level of 21.7% only in gross terms because mall rents are variable. The working-capital release from shrinking inventory (RMB4-5bn over FY2027-28) is real cash but one-off; the engine credits it in those years and nothing thereafter.

scenario_narratives.base: Normalisation, not collapse. Laopu's FY2025 was a once-in-a-category year: SSS +160%, ~RMB1bn per boutique, gold up 55% and the fixed-price product trading at a discount to spot, which pulled investment and reseller demand into a luxury-jewelry P&L. The base case takes FY2026 to ~RMB34bn (H2 slightly below the prior-year H2), lets FY2027 fall 12% as that demand unwinds and gold's 25% correction leaves the brand at a ~60% premium to spot, and then compounds at 5-6% on the things management can control: 10-12 relocations to larger flagship sites, 6-9 overseas stores, goldware, and a 730k-member loyalty base. EBITDA margin resets from the 29.7% H1 FY2026 peak to 24-25%, the FY2024 level. The RMB19bn gold inventory is treated as working capital that stops growing when revenue does; the ~RMB4.2bn of bank debt that funded it is deducted at face.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q2 FY2026 online air-pocket was reseller destocking, end-customer demand (84.6% overlap with LV/Hermes/Cartier buyers) holds, and gold stabilises so the premium-to-spot debate fades. H2 FY2026 grows 12%, there is no FY2027 down year, overseas scales as a second engine and goldware adds a non-wearable category; margins hold 26.5% on flagship productivity. Revenue reaches ~RMB68bn by FY2035, about 2.5x FY2025, which is the sell-side bull framing (JPMorgan, Citi) of a cyclical pause in a structural luxury-brand story. Requires three independent things to go right (demand, gold, overseas), hence the 20% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2025 boom half-reverses. Gold's correction turns the fixed-price model against the company: products look 60% dearer than by-weight gold, price-sensitive and investment-motivated buyers defect, Tmall volumes keep falling, and a China discretionary slowdown lands on top. Revenue falls to ~RMB22bn by FY2028 (still 2.6x FY2024), gross margin drops to ~36% with write-downs on inventory bought at 2025 gold prices, EBITDA margin 18-19%. The company liquidates inventory, which releases RMB4-5bn of cash in FY2027-28 and covers the bank debt, so this is a de-rating bear and not a solvency bear; a further discounted H-share placement to fund inventory would dilute and is the residual risk below this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: single brand and single category, a demand normalisation that is visibly under way (growth 221% -> 60% -> flagged H2 SSS declines; Macquarie Underperform), a fixed-price model that is a two-sided unhedged bet on gold, RMB6.8bn of bank debt against a balance sheet that carried none before the 2024 IPO, and evidence that part of the FY2025 online boom was reseller demand. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs demand, gold and overseas execution to all come right. Base 50%: the H1 FY2026 margin (net 21.5%), loyalty growth and luxury-customer overlap say the franchise is real even if the FY2025 level was not.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Laopu on what a 45-55 boutique Chinese heritage-gold luxury brand earns through a cycle, not on the FY2025 peak and not on the inventory-distorted FY2025 cash flow. The component build normalises revenue down in FY2027, resets EBITDA margin to the FY2024 level, charges the gold inventory as working capital that must be funded whenever revenue grows, treats the capitalised leases as operating cost, discounts in CNY at 10.5% with the same rate in every scenario, caps the terminal multiple at 15x (12x bear) for a cyclical discretionary retailer, and weights the bear at 30%. At roughly 7x trailing earnings the market is already pricing a sharp earnings decline; the finding is where the current price sits relative to the bear path, which is what a buyer is being asked to underwrite.
key_risks_to_valuation: Revenue normalisation deeper than the base -12% FY2027: a quarter of FY2025 demand may have been gold-investment or reseller arbitrage that does not return

Gold price direction, both ways: a further fall widens the fixed-price premium over spot and triggers inventory write-downs on RMB19bn of stock; a sharp rise compresses gross margin until the next list-price increase

Working-capital intensity: inventory at 271 days and ~50% of revenue means any return to growth re-absorbs cash at ~RMB0.45 per RMB1 of revenue, and the wc_capture assumption is the single most value-sensitive driver after the margin
Leverage and dilution: RMB6.8bn of short-term bank borrowings and two discounted H-share placements in 2025; a third placement would dilute the flat share count the model assumes
China discretionary-luxury cyclicality and the HK-listed-China equity risk premium, partly in the 10.5% CNY WACC and partly in the 30% bear weight
Short public history: listed June 2024, one full demand cycle, founder-family control; the normalised margin of 24-25% has never actually been observed on a flat-revenue year
